hints: Look closely at the top circle where the two scales overlap. How many eyepiece graticule units between 10 and 90 line up with the stage micrometer scale?
Remember 1 eyepiece unit is not fixed. You must first find what 1 eyepiece unit equals in mm, then convert to µm, then multiply by the number of eyepiece units covered by the nucleus.
walkthrough:
**Calibrate the eyepiece graticule**

Look at the first diagram. The numbered 0 to 100 scale is the eyepiece graticule which stays in the eyepiece. The bold scale on top is the stage micrometer.

From 10 to 90 on the eyepiece is:
$$90 - 10 = 80 \text{ eyepiece units}$$
This length lines up with 8 small stage divisions. Each small stage division is $0.1 \text{ mm}$.

**Calculate the value of one eyepiece unit**

First find the real length of those 8 stage divisions:
$$8 \times 0.1 \text{ mm} = 0.8 \text{ mm}$$
So 80 eyepiece units = 0.8 mm.
$$1 \text{ eyepiece unit} = 0.8 / 80 = 0.01 \text{ mm}$$
Convert mm to micrometres. Remember $1 \text{ mm} = 1000 \text{ } \mu\text{m}$:
$$0.01 \text{ mm} \times 1000 = 10 \text{ } \mu\text{m}$$
So at this magnification, 1 eyepiece unit = 10 µm.

**Measure the nucleus and convert**

Now look at the plant cell photo with the same eyepiece scale underneath. The dark round nucleus on the right covers about 2.5 eyepiece units.
$$2.5 \times 10 \text{ } \mu\text{m} = 25 \text{ } \mu\text{m}$$
That is a sensible size for a plant nucleus, not mm size.

options.A: 0.8 mm is the total calibrated length for 80 eyepiece units, not the nucleus. It is also far too large for a nucleus and uses the wrong units.
options.B: 8 µm would be less than 1 eyepiece unit at 10 µm per unit. The nucleus clearly covers more than 2 eyepiece units.
options.C: About 2.5 eyepiece units x 10 µm per unit = 25 µm, which matches the measured nucleus length.
options.D: 200 µm is about 20 eyepiece units. That is close to a whole cell length, not the small nucleus.
